slot.brief: Give a particle's position vector and angular velocity (or force) in component form and ask for the torque/angular momentum vector using the cross product.

stem: A particle of mass $1$ kg has position vector $(1,2,3)$ m and velocity $(2,-1,1)$ m s$^{-1}$. Its angular momentum about the origin, in component form, is
working:
$\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v=(1,2,3)\times(2,-1,1)$
$\mathbf L=(2+3,\ 6-1,\ -1-4)=(5,5,-5)\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$

Independent check: \(\mathbf L=m(\mathbf r\times\mathbf v)=(2-3(-1),\;3\cdot2-1,\;-1-4)=(5,5,-5)\).
solution:
Angular momentum is $\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v$. Thus,
$$\mathbf L=(1,2,3)\times(2,-1,1)=(5,5,-5)\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}.$$
